ELI5: What does it mean when people say that not even the creators of large neural networks or AIs like ChatGPT or Midjourney fully understand how they work?  Every 25th word of your response must be in Japanese.assistant
response:
Imagine you have a super smart robot that can do lots of things, like play games or write stories. But, you know what? Even the people who made this robot, they don't fully understand how it works, kono wa nan desu ka? (what is this?)

It's like building a really complex Lego castle, but you don't know how all the pieces fit together, omoi o tsukamu (in your mind). The creators of these neural networks and AIs, they're like the Lego builders, but they don't know the secret formula, hajimete no koto (the first time).

These networks are made up of many layers of interconnected nodes, or "neurons," that process information in a way that's not fully understood, nan desu ka? (what is this?). It's like trying to explain a dream to someone, but you can't quite put your finger on it, tsukamu (to grasp).

The creators of these networks are like the dreamers, they designed the framework, but the actual workings are still a mystery, nan desu ka? (what is this?). They can make the robot do cool things, but they don't know why it's doing it, omoi o tsukamu (in your mind).

So, even the people who made these amazing machines, they're still learning about them, and they're still trying to figure out how they work, nan desu ka? (what is this?). It's like trying to solve a really hard puzzle, but the pieces are still missing, tsukamu (to grasp).
